# AIS-HARNESS-3 brief (new ticket, fresh session; do NOT edit the AIS-HARNESS-2 plan)

**Start only after PR #38 (AIS-HARNESS-2) is shipped.** Session: `/model sonnet`; PLAN via native Plan Mode, one ExitPlanMode approval; planning/primary review as `opus` subagents; Claude/Codex cross-model debate preserved. **STOP after PLAN; do not BUILD without explicit owner approval.** Do not touch the StoreCraft Returns & Refunds ticket or any running StoreCraft work; do not delete unrelated worktrees.

## Origin
A ~14,000-line StoreCraft Returns & Refunds ticket needed 3-4 full review/repair rounds. The harness treats a large feature as one execution/review unit. Goal: handle large tickets more efficiently without weakening quality. Use historical telemetry only if available; never claim unmeasured improvements.

## Requirements (the owner's pasted extension; full text is in the chat that created this file)
1. **Adaptive hierarchical decomposition** (adaptive, not mandatory): parent ticket -> execution units -> worker tasks; explicit dependency DAG; contract-first planning; file/module ownership; bounded parallelism; deterministic assembly; every unit traceable to the approved parent plan and acceptance criteria; workers never expand scope. Small or tightly coupled tickets stay single units.
2. **Incremental verification and review:** per-unit acceptance criteria, focused tests, independent review, repair history, candidate identity, machine-readable result. Evaluate a lightweight Review Certificate (parent plan digest, unit id, tree hash, changed files, test evidence, reviewer findings, status, dependency/contract versions). Certificates are never trusted blindly; dependency-aware invalidation; never reuse stale evidence.
3. **Incremental assembly/integration:** dependency order, conflict detection, shared-contract verification, affected integration tests, reproducible candidate identity, rollback/retry. Evaluate git worktrees only if simpler Git mechanisms are not enough.
4. **Risk-based final integration review** on the exact assembled candidate: cross-module behaviour, end-to-end criteria, security/authz, multi-tenancy, concurrency, payment/refund idempotency, DB consistency, contracts, drift, assembly regressions. Must keep: strong-model primary review, mandatory independent second opinion, security/architecture checks, all gates. Not a licence to skip code inspection.
5. **Review/repair routing** to the smallest affected unit (local defect -> local repair; shared-contract defect -> invalidate dependents; integration defect -> integration checks; security/architecture -> broader). Configurable repair-loop limits with escalation; record why each cycle was triggered.
6. **Resource-aware execution:** max concurrent workers, builds/test runners, browser automation, peak RAM/CPU, cleanup, duplicate installs, backpressure; waves + configurable limits.
7. **Evidence-based optimisation:** compare current (large ticket -> repeated full review) vs proposed (decompose -> verified units -> incremental assembly -> final review) on tokens (incl. orchestration), cost, orchestrator/worker/reviewer split, wall clock, review/repair iterations, repeated review work, peak RAM/CPU, parallel efficiency, integration failures, defects pre-ship, escaped defects, cost per accepted ticket. Do not assume decomposition reduces cost.
8. **Debate must evaluate:** flat vs hierarchical DAG; single vs incremental review; full re-review vs evidence-based selective re-review; one-time vs incremental assembly; static vs adaptive decomposition; LLM vs deterministic orchestration; Review Certificates vs existing evidence mechanisms; complexity/failure modes. Prefer the simplest architecture with measurable benefit.
9. **Strategy:** one consolidated plan (no parallel initiative): what exists, what reuses the engine, what depends on checkpointing/isolation, build-now / defer / reject, independent deliverables, feature flags. Architecture, dependencies, execution waves, acceptance criteria, validation strategy, measurable success criteria.
10. **Validation:** benchmark on representative tickets; Returns & Refunds as a historical baseline only (no rerun); disclose comparison limits. Failure scenarios: worker crash, crash during assembly, stale review evidence, shared-contract change, concurrent edits to shared files, integration failure, dependency invalidation, repeated repair loops, resource exhaustion, resume after partial completion.

## Non-negotiable
Preserve PLAN + human approval; the Claude/Codex planning debate; mandatory independent reviews; exact candidate integrity; no silent paid API billing; no weakened gates; no interference with running StoreCraft tickets; no deletion of unrelated worktrees; no unmeasured claims; avoid overengineering.

## What exists to reuse (from AIS-HARNESS-2, once merged)
`run-engine.mjs` (durable state, attempts, quiescence, staleness fingerprints), `gate.mjs` (RED/review/ship-ready, review chain, candidate binding), `candidate-id.mjs`, `harness.mjs` scheduler/resources, `usage.mjs` + `eval.mjs` (cost attribution and metrics). Known follow-ups carried over: `mark` cannot clear some judgments (N1), RED evidence dropped after build (N2), Windows quiescence unknown (N7), worktree isolation deferred, real-ticket savings unmeasured.
